explanation: Indirect value of biodiversity is based on services ecosystems perform simply by existing. These services include biogeochemical cycling, waste recycling, provision of fresh water, prevention of soil erosion, climate regulation, and ecotourism. Biogeochemical cycles: diverse ecosystems maintain water, carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus cycles, which provide fresh water, remove CO2 from the atmosphere, absorb excess soil nitrogen, and supply phosphate. Waste recycling: decomposers recycle dead organic matter and wastes into inorganic nutrients for producers. This prevents the millions of tons of waste dumped by humans annually from accumulating and covering the entire surface of the Earth.

questions.q: What would happen to human waste without the recycling function of decomposers?
opts: It would turn into fossil fuel reservoirs immediately.
It would soon cover the entire surface of the Earth.
It would evaporate through stomata as gaseous nitrogen.
It would be converted into essential amino acids by plants.
